Retired West Seneca school psychologist charged in child porn case

A recently retired psychologist in the West Seneca schools is facing child pornography charges.

David M. Calaiacovo, 61, of Hamburg appeared in Buffalo federal court Wednesday to face allegations that he received and possessed sexually explicit photos of underage girls.

Calaiacovo was arrested after a search of his home on Wayfare Court last week resulted in the seizure of a laptop containing child pornography, according to the complaint against him.

The complaint said Calaiacovo spoke to Homeland Security investigators at the time of the search and said he had been in the psychology field for 35 years and had retired from West Seneca schools the day before.

In court papers, investigators detail the photos found in the laptop, including one with a young girl in a school setting.

"The female child is in the middle of the picture with what appears to be a classroom setting that includes a painted background of books on a shelf and a chalkboard," the court papers state. "The photo also includes a globe, chair, desk, abacus and pencils on the floor with the child."

Investigators said the tip that led to his arrest came from the State Police and the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children.

“The government is concerned because this defendant worked in the elementary schools for 35 years and had access to children,” said Assistant U.S. Attorney Meghan Tokash.

Tokash, during a court appearance Wednesday, acknowledged that at this point there is no evidence of a link between his job with the schools and the child porn allegations.

Calaiacovo is charged with receipt and possession of child pornography.
